fix: Replace the two silent casts with checked conversions and reject out-of-range ids as stale: let (Ok(index), Ok(generation)) = (u32::try_from(window.index().saturating_sub(1)), u32::try_from(window.generation())) else { return Err(incular_devtools_protocol::ErrorCode::StaleId); }; then let id = WindowId::from_parts(index, generation);

Check emptiness and move the root out instead of cloning it: if nodes.is_empty() { return Err(incular_devtools_protocol::ErrorCode::UnknownId); } let root = nodes.remove(0); (remove the later nodes.remove(0) line). Keeps the same order of the remaining nodes.

Use an iterator adapter: registry.slots.iter_mut().filter_map(|slot| slot.record.as_mut()).any(|record| record.runtime.devtools_edit_property(id, name, value)). Apply the same change to devtools_revert_property (loop at line 827), keeping the early-exit semantics of any().

Stop allocating a Vec<WindowId> just to iterate live windows: borrow the registry once and walk its records directly (let registry = self.registry.borrow(); for slot in &registry.slots { let Some(record) = slot.record.as_ref() else { continue }; ... }). Same pattern in devtools_node_bounds (line 844) and devtools_node_overlay_geometry (line 870), which the selected-node overlay may call per frame.

Return a borrow instead of an owned clone: pub fn launch_activation(&self) -> &LaunchActivation { &self.launch_activation }. Callers that need ownership call .clone() themselves. This is a breaking signature change for a doc(hidden) API, so record it in the CHANGELOG if adopted.
Add #[must_use] to this draining accessor (take_native_application_shell_requests) so that callers cannot silently drop the drained requests.
